response.title: which power station recharges fastest from the car while driving
response.answer:
The fastest portable power stations to recharge while driving are generally EcoFlow and BLUETTI models paired with dedicated alternator chargers.

The key is the charging method:

Regular 12V cigarette lighter: Usually 100–120W, sometimes up to 240W.

Dedicated alternator charger: Typically 500–1,000W, with some newer systems offering even higher charging rates.

That means a 1,000Wh power station could take 10+ hours through a cigarette lighter but roughly 1–2 hours with a high-power alternator charger.

The important distinction is that the fastest-charging power station isn't necessarily the one with the fastest car-charging capability.

search_results.snippet: The Verge reviews EcoFlow’s $599 Alternator Charger, a device that connects a vehicle’s starter battery to compatible EcoFlow power stations, delivering up to 800W while driving. This can charge a 1kWh Delta 3 in just over an hour and a 4kWh Delta Pro 3 in about five hours, while also supporting reverse charging to maintain or jump-start the vehicle’s battery. The charger regulates output to avoid overloading the alternator and can combine with solar panels for more than 1,100W of charging. Installation is manageable as a DIY project but requires substantial wiring and vehicle-specific work. I
